title: Avoid the use of the "root" account
description: An Alibaba Cloud account can be viewed as a "root" account. The "root" account has full control permissions to all cloud products and resources under such account. It is highly recommended that the use of this account should be avoided. The "root" account is the owner of the resources under an Alibaba Cloud account. This account pays for and has full control permissions to resources. Reported as a manual review item: the benchmark audit needs console review or organisational judgement.
reference: CIS Alibaba Cloud Foundation Benchmark v2.0.1 - 1.1 Avoid the use of the "root" account

audit.command: You can enable ActionTrail for your account, and create a trail to deliver all action logs to Alibaba Cloud Log Service. Then, you can enable an alarm to discover the usage of "root" account and receive notifications on those conditions. Implement the Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for usage of "root" account recommendation in the Logging and Monitoring section to receive notifications of root account usage.

remediation.command: All users should operate resources at the RAM user level and follow the principle of least privilege. Follow the remediation instructions of the Ensure RAM policies are attached only to groups or roles recommendation. For more information about RAM user, see terms of RAM user.

title: Ensure MFA is enabled for the "root" account
description: With MFA enabled, anytime the "root" account logs on to Alibaba Cloud, it will be prompted for username and password followed by an authentication code from the virtual MFA device. It is recommended that MFA be enabled for the "root" user. It is important to prevent "root" account from being compromised. Enabling MFA requires the "root" account holder to provide additional information on top of username and password. Reported as a manual review item: the benchmark audit needs console review or organisational judgement.
reference: CIS Alibaba Cloud Foundation Benchmark v2.0.1 - 1.3 Ensure MFA is enabled for the "root" account

audit.command: Perform the following to determine if an MFA device is enabled for the "root" account: Using the management console: 1. Logon to RAM console by using your Alibaba Cloud account (root account). 2. In the left-side navigation pane, click Overview. 3. In the Security Check section, make sure that Enable MFA for Root Account is marked as Finished.

remediation.command: Perform the following to enable MFA for "root" account Using the management console: 1. Logon to RAM console by using your Alibaba Cloud account (root account). 2. Move the pointer over the account icon in the upper-right corner and click Security Settings. 3. In the Account Protection section, Click Edit. 4. On the displayed page, select a scenario and select TOTP. 5. Click Submit. 6. On the displayed page, click Verify now. 7. Enter the verification code and click Submit. 8. Download and install a mobile application that supports TOTP MFA, such as Google Authenticator, on your mobile phone. Note: If you already installed Google Authenticator, click Next.

title: Ensure that multi-factor authentication is enabled for all RAM users that have a console password
description: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) adds an extra layer of protection on top of a username and password. With MFA enabled, when a user logs on to Alibaba Cloud, they will be prompted for their user name and password followed by an authentication code from their virtual MFA device. MFA requires users to verify their identities by entering two authentication factors. When MFA is enabled, an attacker faces at least two different authentication mechanisms. Every RAM user with a login profile (console access) must have an MFA device (GetUserMFAInfo). Read-only aliyun CLI calls; credentials and default region come from the CLI's normal profile (aliyun configure, ~/.aliyun/config.json or ALIBABA_CLOUD_* environment variables). JSON output is parsed with sed/awk. A missing CLI or credential fails the check.
reference: CIS Alibaba Cloud Foundation Benchmark v2.0.1 - 1.4 Ensure that multi-factor authentication is enabled for all RAM users that have a console password

audit.command:
out=$(aliyun ram ListUsers --MaxItems 1000 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
users=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/.*"UserName"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
bad=0
for u in $users; do
  if err=$(aliyun ram GetLoginProfile --UserName "$u" 2>&1); then
    if ! err=$(aliyun ram GetUserMFAInfo --UserName "$u" 2>&1); then
      printf '%s\n' "$err" | grep -q EntityNotExist || exit 1
      echo "no MFA: $u"; bad=1
    fi
  else
    printf '%s\n' "$err" | grep -q EntityNotExist || exit 1
  fi
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: Have each listed user bind a virtual MFA device (RAM console > Identities > Users > Authentication > Enable MFA) and require it: aliyun ram UpdateLoginProfile --UserName <u> --MFABindRequired true.

title: Ensure RAM policies that allow full "*:*" administrative privileges are not created
description: RAM policies represent permissions that can be granted to users, groups, or roles. It is recommended and considered a standard security advice to grant least privilege-that is, granting only the permissions required to perform tasks. It is more secure to start with a minimum set of permissions and grant additional permissions as necessary, rather than starting with permissions that exceed the necessity and then trying to tighten them later. Flags custom policies with AttachmentCount > 0 whose default version has a statement with Effect Allow, Action "*" and Resource "*". Read-only aliyun CLI calls; credentials and default region come from the CLI's normal profile (aliyun configure, ~/.aliyun/config.json or ALIBABA_CLOUD_* environment variables). JSON output is parsed with sed/awk. A missing CLI or credential fails the check.
reference: CIS Alibaba Cloud Foundation Benchmark v2.0.1 - 1.15 Ensure RAM policies that allow full "*:*" administrative privileges are not created

audit.command:
out=$(aliyun ram ListPolicies --PolicyType Custom --MaxItems 1000 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
pols=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/.*"PolicyName"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | sort -u)
bad=0
for p in $pols; do
  g=$(aliyun ram GetPolicy --PolicyName "$p" --PolicyType Custom 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
  n=$(printf '%s\n' "$g" | sed -n 's/.*"AttachmentCount"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\([0-9]\{1,\}\).*/\1/p' | head -n 1)
  [ "${n:-0}" -gt 0 ] || continue
  doc=$(printf '%s\n' "$g" | grep '"PolicyDocument"' | head -n 1 | sed 's/\\n//g; s/\\t//g; s/\\"/"/g' | tr -d ' \t')
  if printf '%s\n' "$doc" | tr '{}' '\n\n' | grep '"Effect":"Allow"' | grep -E '"Action":(\["\*"\]|"\*")' | grep -Eq '"Resource":(\["\*"\]|"\*")'; then
    echo "attached full-admin policy: $p"; bad=1
  fi
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: Detach the listed policies from all identities (aliyun ram DetachPolicyFromUser/Group/Role) and replace them with least-privilege policies; use the system AdministratorAccess policy only for a small, controlled group.

title: Ensure the OSS used to store ActionTrail logs is not publicly accessible
description: ActionTrail logs a record of every API call made in your Alibaba Cloud account. These logs file are stored in an OSS bucket. It is recommended that the access control list (ACL) of the OSS bucket, which ActionTrail logs to, shall prevent public access to the ActionTrail logs. Allowing public access to ActionTrail log content may aid an adversary in identifying weaknesses in the affected account's use or configuration. Every OSS bucket that a trail delivers to (OssBucketName) must have ACL private (aliyun oss stat). Read-only aliyun CLI calls; credentials and default region come from the CLI's normal profile (aliyun configure, ~/.aliyun/config.json or ALIBABA_CLOUD_* environment variables). JSON output is parsed with sed/awk. A missing CLI or credential fails the check.
reference: CIS Alibaba Cloud Foundation Benchmark v2.0.1 - 2.2 Ensure the OSS used to store ActionTrail logs is not publicly accessible

audit.command:
out=$(aliyun actiontrail DescribeTrails 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
bs=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/.*"OssBucketName"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]\{1,\}\)".*/\1/p' | sort -u)
bad=0
for b in $bs; do
  st=$(aliyun oss stat "oss://$b" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
  acl=$(printf '%s\n' "$st" | sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*ACL[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\([^[:space:]]*\).*/\1/p' | head -n 1)
  [ "$acl" = private ] || { echo "trail bucket ACL $acl: $b"; bad=1; }
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: aliyun oss set-acl oss://<bucket> private -b for each listed bucket and review its bucket policy for anonymous grants.

title: Ensure that 'Unattached disks' are encrypted
description: Ensure that unattached disks in a subscription are encrypted. Cloud disk encryption protects your data at rest. The cloud disk data encryption feature automatically encrypts data when data is transferred from ECS instances to disks, and decrypts data when the data is read from ... Counts disks with Status Available (unattached) and Encrypted false in every ECS region; the count must be 0. Read-only aliyun CLI calls; credentials and default region come from the CLI's normal profile (aliyun configure, ~/.aliyun/config.json or ALIBABA_CLOUD_* environment variables). JSON output is parsed with sed/awk. A missing CLI or credential fails the check.
reference: CIS Alibaba Cloud Foundation Benchmark v2.0.1 - 4.1 Ensure that 'Unattached disks' are encrypted

audit.command:
regs=$(aliyun ecs DescribeRegions 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
regions=$(printf '%s\n' "$regs" | sed -n 's/.*"RegionId"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | sort -u)
[ -n "$regions" ] || exit 1
bad=0
for r in $regions; do
  out=$(aliyun ecs DescribeDisks --RegionId "$r" --Status Available --Encrypted false --PageSize 10 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
  n=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/.*"TotalCount"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\([0-9]\{1,\}\).*/\1/p' | head -n 1)
  [ "${n:-0}" -eq 0 ] || { echo "unencrypted unattached disks in $r: $n"; bad=1; }
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: Encrypted cannot be switched on for an existing disk: create an encrypted snapshot copy / encrypted disk from a snapshot (aliyun ecs CopySnapshot --Encrypted true, CreateDisk --Encrypted true --KMSKeyId <key>), swap it in, and enable account-level default EBS encryption for new disks.

title: Ensure no security groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to port 22
description: Security groups provide stateful filtering of ingress/egress network traffic to Alibaba Cloud resources. It is recommended that no security group allows unrestricted ingress access to port 22. [ -n "$regions" ] || exit 1
bad=0
for r in $regions; do
  page=1
  while :; do

    ids=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/.*"DBInstanceId"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | sort -u)

    done
    set -- $ids
    [ "$#" -lt 100 ] && break
    page=$((page + 1))
  done
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

title: Ensure users not logged on for 90 days or longer are disabled for console logon
description: Alibaba Cloud RAM users can logon to Alibaba Cloud console by using their user name and password. If a user has not logged on for 90 days or longer, it is recommended to disable the console access of the user. Disabling users from having unnecessary logon privileges will reduce the opportunity that an abandoned user or a user with compromised password to be used. For each RAM user with console access, LastLoginDate (or CreateDate when the user never signed in) must be less than 90 days old. Uses GNU date -d. Read-only aliyun CLI calls; credentials and default region come from the CLI's normal profile (aliyun configure, ~/.aliyun/config.json or ALIBABA_CLOUD_* environment variables). JSON output is parsed with sed/awk. A missing CLI or credential fails the check.
reference: CIS Alibaba Cloud Foundation Benchmark v2.0.1 - 1.5 Ensure users not logged on for 90 days or longer are disabled for console logon

audit.command:
now=$(date -u +%s) || exit 1
out=$(aliyun ram ListUsers --MaxItems 1000 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
users=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/.*"UserName"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
bad=0
for u in $users; do
  if err=$(aliyun ram GetLoginProfile --UserName "$u" 2>&1); then
    g=$(aliyun ram GetUser --UserName "$u" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
    d=$(printf '%s\n' "$g" | sed -n 's/.*"LastLoginDate"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]\{1,\}\)".*/\1/p' | head -n 1)
    [ -n "$d" ] || d=$(printf '%s\n' "$g" | sed -n 's/.*"CreateDate"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]\{1,\}\)".*/\1/p' | head -n 1)
    ts=$(date -u -d "$d" +%s 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
    [ $(( (now - ts) / 86400 )) -lt 90 ] || { echo "no console logon for 90+ days: $u"; bad=1; }
  else
    printf '%s\n' "$err" | grep -q EntityNotExist || exit 1
  fi
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

title: Ensure legacy networks does not exist
description: In order to prevent use of legacy networks, ECS instances should not have a legacy network configured. Legacy networks have a single network IPv4 prefix range and a single gateway IP address for the whole network. With legacy networks, you cannot create subnetworks or switch from legacy to auto or custom subnet networks. Counts ECS instances with InstanceNetworkType classic in every region; any instance on the legacy classic network fails. Read-only aliyun CLI calls; credentials and default region come from the CLI's normal profile (aliyun configure, ~/.aliyun/config.json or ALIBABA_CLOUD_* environment variables). JSON output is parsed with sed/awk. A missing CLI or credential fails the check.
reference: CIS Alibaba Cloud Foundation Benchmark v2.0.1 - 3.1 Ensure legacy networks does not exist

audit.command:
regs=$(aliyun ecs DescribeRegions 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
regions=$(printf '%s\n' "$regs" | sed -n 's/.*"RegionId"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | sort -u)
[ -n "$regions" ] || exit 1
bad=0
for r in $regions; do
  out=$(aliyun ecs DescribeInstances --RegionId "$r" --InstanceNetworkType classic --PageSize 10 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
  n=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/.*"TotalCount"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\([0-9]\{1,\}\).*/\1/p' | head -n 1)
  [ "${n:-0}" -eq 0 ] || { echo "classic-network instances in $r: $n"; bad=1; }
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: Migrate classic-network ECS instances to a VPC (ECS console > Instances > Migrate to VPC) and stop creating classic-network resources.

title: Ensure automatic rotation is enabled for customer created symmetric KMS keys
description: Automatic rotation limits the amount of data protected by one key version. In the profile's region, every Enabled symmetric (Aliyun_AES_256 / Aliyun_SM4) key created by the account must have AutomaticRotation Enabled; service-created default keys are skipped. Read-only aliyun CLI calls; credentials and default region come from the CLI's normal profile (aliyun configure, ~/.aliyun/config.json or ALIBABA_CLOUD_* environment variables). JSON output is parsed with grep/sed/awk. A missing CLI or credential fails the check.
reference: CIS Alibaba Cloud Foundation Benchmark - Logging and Monitoring - KMS key rotation (verify section number for your release)

audit.command:
out=$(aliyun kms ListKeys --PageSize 100 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
keys=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/.*"KeyId"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
get() { printf '%s\n' "$m" | sed -n "s/.*\"$1\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"\([^\"]*\)\".*/\1/p" | head -n 1; }
bad=0
for k in $keys; do
  m=$(aliyun kms DescribeKey --KeyId "$k" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
  case "$(get KeySpec)" in ''|Aliyun_AES_256|Aliyun_SM4) ;; *) continue ;; esac
  [ "$(get KeyState)" = Enabled ] || continue
  case "$(get Creator)" in ''|*[!0-9]*) continue ;; esac
  [ "$(get AutomaticRotation)" = Enabled ] || { echo "rotation off: $k"; bad=1; }
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: aliyun kms UpdateRotationPolicy --KeyId <key-id> --EnableAutomaticRotation true --RotationInterval 31536000s (or a shorter interval) for each listed key.
